title: Operational quasiprobability formulation of non-signaling in time for macrorealism violations
abstract: In this paper, we introduce the concept of quasi non-signaling in time (QNSIT), which extends non-signaling in time (NSIT) to quasiprobability distributions. QNSIT requires that the marginals of the quasiprobability distribution under consideration at intermediate times remain unperturbed by the measurement back-action induced by a sequence of quantum measurements. Associated with QNSIT, we propose a quasiprobabilistic characterization of macrorealism, ${\rm MR}_{\rm qp}$, which requires that both the QNSIT conditions are satisfied and the quasiprobability distribution constructed from the measurement outcomes is positive. We prove that ${\rm MR}_{\rm qp}$ implies NSIT, whereas the converse does not hold because of hidden superposition paths generated or preserved by the system dynamics. We also prove that, for a two-level system, the ${\rm MR}_{\rm qp}$ and NSIT conditions coincide. ${\rm MR}_{\rm qp}$ therefore provides a more sensitive tool for testing macrorealism and can be implemented experimentally through a quantum non-demolition measurement scheme.
summary: This paper introduces Quasi non-signaling in time (QNSIT) and a corresponding quasiprobabilistic criterion for macrorealism ($	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$). It demonstrates that $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$ is a stricter test than standard Non-Signaling in Time (NSIT), offering a more sensitive tool to detect violations of macrorealism, particularly through quantum non-demolition measurements.
main_problem: To develop a more sensitive operational test for macrorealism violations than the standard Non-Signaling in Time (NSIT) conditions.
main_result: The proposed criterion, $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$, is strictly stronger than NSIT, although for two-level systems, it becomes equivalent to the standard macrorealism condition ($	ext{MR}_{	ext{str}}$).
method: The authors introduce a quasiprobabilistic characterization of macrorealism ($	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$) based on a real multi-time quasiprobability density function $P(\Omega)$.
model_or_system: The analysis considers a general quantum system undergoing sequential measurements at distinct times ($t_0, t_1, t_2$), involving system and detector degrees of freedom.
key_observables: The quasiprobability distribution $P(\Omega)$ and its positivity, which serves as the diagnostic tool for $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$.
important_parameters: The system Hamiltonian, measurement projectors $\{\hat{\Pi}(X)\}$, and the time evolution operators $\hat{U}$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on extending the concept to quasiprobabilities and assuming the validity of the QNSIT conditions, which are shown to be always satisfied.
paper_structure: The paper introduces QNSIT and $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$, proves $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}} \implies 	ext{NSIT}$, and then analyzes the conditions under which the equivalence holds, showing the strictness of $	ext{MR}_{	ext{qp}}$ in general dimensions.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, operational framework using quasiprobabilities to test fundamental assumptions about physical reality (macrorealism) in time, which is crucial for understanding the limits of classical descriptions of quantum measurements.
